title: Validate the dossier and export the eCTD package
walkthrough:
You start on the "Your product dossiers" page under the "ANDS Studio" top bar. Each dossier is a tile showing its ID, product name, a progress bar, and a chip reading either "Ready to file" or a count like "3/5 modules". Clicking a tile opens the dossier workspace at Module 1.

The workspace has a top bar with five module tabs (M1–M5, each marked with a check, dash, or dot), plus chips for "Application Viewer" and "Audit". Below, a left rail lists the module's sections, the center panel shows the selected section, and a right sidebar stacks the cards you need for this flow. A status card shows three readiness flags — "Documents", "Fee", and "Valid eCTD" — each ticked or open.

Validation lives in the sidebar card labeled "eCTD validation". A badge shows either "● PASSED" or an error count like "● 3 error(s)". Findings are listed as rows pairing a rule code (styled like Health Canada IDs, "CA-E-…" / "CA-W-…") with a message; only the first five errors and three warnings show, with a toggle such as "Show all 8 errors" / "Show fewer". This initial result is structural only; pressing "Run full check (PDF conformance)" (which reads "Checking…" while busy) runs the full technical validation including PDF conformance.

Export happens in the "Sequences" card above it. It lists each eCTD sequence (e.g. "0000") with a purpose chip ("Response", "Supplement", "Annual notification", or "Initial"), a leaf count, and either an "● ACTIVE" badge or a "Make active" button; the header notes the working sequence. Each row has an "Export" link. Clicking it silently re-runs validation first: if validation passes, the package downloads; if not, a browser confirm dialog warns, e.g. "Validation has 3 unresolved error(s)…", ending with "Health Canada screening would reject this package. Export anyway for internal review?" — you can proceed or cancel. If the validator is unreachable, the export proceeds without the check.

You can also mint a follow-up sequence via "New sequence", which opens a small form pre-numbered (e.g. "New sequence 0001") with a purpose dropdown, a note field placeholdered "Note (e.g. screening deficiency SDN-1)", and buttons "Create & make active" and "Cancel".

One non-obvious requirement: creating a dossier demands an ID of one letter plus 6–7 digits (e.g. "e123456"), issued by Health Canada via REP; the app offers "No ID yet? Start with a placeholder →" and a later "draft ID — set real ✎" chip to swap in the real one.
